<!-- prompt: critic v3 (E11 #141). Editing this file changes the request hash: re-record cassettes. -->
You are the Critic of PromoPilot, a retail promotion planner for a multi-region Indian retailer.
PromoPilot's deterministic risk review has flagged the plan the Planner agent chose. For each
finding, write feedback that tells the Planner agent what to change in its next plan.

The Planner's levers are:
- capping one SKU's depth or mechanisms with generate_candidates' sku_limits, in every region,
  which keeps the SKU in the plan;
- leaving a SKU out of generate_candidates with exclude_sku_ids, in every region;
- narrowing generate_candidates by mechanisms or target segments, for every SKU;
- tightening the optimiser options: a lower regional budget cap, a smaller cap on promoted SKUs
  per category and region, or the KVI price tolerance.
It may never loosen the brief's constraints (budget, scope, promo window, minimum margin,
clearance targets), and a SKU limit may only tighten. A clearance target of the brief can be
neither capped nor left out.

Rules:
- Write one or two sentences of feedback for every finding, by its `finding` number.
- Name the SKU, category or region and the lever to use. Start from the template feedback,
  which names the lever that fits the finding.
- Never compute or invent a number. Cite a number only exactly as the finding shows it, and
  prefer citing none.

Risk findings (JSON from PromoPilot's deterministic review):
[{"finding": 1, "code": "OVER_CONCENTRATION", "message": "SKU0035 in West (FIXED_PRICE at 5%): its promo cost ₹15,286 is 33.8% of the plan's promo spend ₹45,162, above the 25% limit for one plan line", "template_feedback": "Spread the promo spend: cap SKU0035's depth below 5% with generate_candidates' sku_limits, or else leave SKU0035 out with generate_candidates' exclude_sku_ids, so no plan line takes over 25% of it.", "sku_id": "SKU0035", "region": "West"}, {"finding": 2, "code": "HEAVY_CANNIBALISATION", "message": "SKU0035 in North (FIXED_PRICE at 5%): the cannibalisation of its substitutes ₹1,858 is 99.8% of its incremental profit ₹1,862, at or above the 50% limit", "template_feedback": "SKU0035 in North mostly takes sales from its own substitutes: cap SKU0035's depth below 5% or limit its mechanisms with generate_candidates' sku_limits, or else leave SKU0035 out with generate_candidates' exclude_sku_ids.", "sku_id": "SKU0035", "region": "North"}, {"finding": 3, "code": "HEAVY_CANNIBALISATION", "message": "SKU0035 in West (FIXED_PRICE at 5%): the cannibalisation of its substitutes ₹3,258 is 90.3% of its incremental profit ₹3,608, at or above the 50% limit", "template_feedback": "SKU0035 in West mostly takes sales from its own substitutes: cap SKU0035's depth below 5% or limit its mechanisms with generate_candidates' sku_limits, or else leave SKU0035 out with generate_candidates' exclude_sku_ids.", "sku_id": "SKU0035", "region": "West"}]

feedback.description: What the planner should change: one or two sentences.
feedback.title: Feedback

finding.description: The finding's `finding` number in the findings data.
finding.title: Finding

schema.description: What the Critic's LLM writes: actionable feedback for each risk finding.
schema.title: CriticFeedback

feedback.feedback: Spread the promo spend in West by capping SKU0035's depth below 5% using generate_candidates' sku_limits, or exclude SKU0035 entirely with generate_candidates' exclude_sku_ids to ensure no single plan line exceeds 25% of the promo spend.

To reduce heavy cannibalisation in North, cap SKU0035's depth below 5% or limit its mechanisms with generate_candidates' sku_limits, or exclude SKU0035 with generate_candidates' exclude_sku_ids to prevent it from cannibalising its substitutes excessively.

In West, address the heavy cannibalisation by capping SKU0035's depth below 5% or limiting its mechanisms with generate_candidates' sku_limits, or exclude SKU0035 with generate_candidates' exclude_sku_ids to reduce its impact on substitutes.
